papers.title: Batch Me If You Can: Coverage-guided RPKI Fuzzing at Scale
papers.abstract: The Resource Public Key Infrastructure (RPKI) has become essential to secure inter-domain routing. Despite its critical role, RPKI software remains largely untested beyond shallow parsing. Existing fuzzers, like AFL++ or libFuzzer, do not work well for protocol fuzzing at scale.

papers.title: Quality-Assured Fuzz Harness Generation via the Four Principles Framework
papers.abstract: Fuzz testing is the dominant technique for finding memory-safety vulnerabilities in C/C++ software, yet its effectiveness hinges on the quality of fuzz harnesses. We propose the Four Principles Framework for quality-assured fuzz harness generation.

papers.title: PickleFuzzer: A Case Study in Fuzzing for Discrepancies Between Python Pickle Implementations
papers.abstract: Python's native serialization protocol, pickle, is a powerful but insecure format for transferring untrusted data. It is frequently used, especially for saving machine learning models, despite known security risks.

papers.title: AFL-ICP: Enhancing Industrial Control Protocol Reliability via Specification-Guided Fuzzing
papers.abstract: Industrial Control Protocols (ICPs) are critical to the reliability and stability of industrial infrastructure. We present AFL-ICP, a specification-guided fuzzing framework that enhances ICP reliability by leveraging protocol specifications to generate semantically valid test inputs.

papers.title: From CRUD to Autonomous Agents: Formal Validation and Zero-Trust Security for Semantic Gateways in AI-Native Enterprise Systems
papers.abstract: Enterprise systems are shifting away from deterministic CRUD/REST architectures toward AI-native systems where large language models act as cognitive orchestrators. This transition introduces a critical security tension: probabilistic LLMs weaken classical mechanisms for validation.

papers.title: ARIstoteles -- Dissecting Apple's Baseband Interface
papers.abstract: Wireless chips and interfaces expose a substantial remote attack surface. Most cellular baseband security research is performed on the Android ecosystem, leaving a huge gap on Apple devices. With iOS jailbreaks, last-generation wireless interfaces are now accessible.

papers.title: Auditing MCP Servers for Over-Privileged Tool Capabilities
papers.abstract: The Model Context Protocol (MCP) has emerged as a standard for connecting Large Language Models to external tools and data. However, MCP servers often expose privileged capabilities such as file system access, network requests, and command execution without appropriate access control.

papers.title: Coverage-Guided Multi-Agent Harness Generation for Java Library Fuzzing
papers.abstract: Coverage-guided fuzzing has proven effective for software testing, but targeting library code requires specialized harnesses. We present a multi-agent system for automated fuzz harness generation for Java libraries.

papers.title: SemFuzz: A Semantics-Aware Fuzzing Framework for Network Protocol Implementations
papers.abstract: Network protocols are the foundation of modern communication, yet their implementations often contain semantic vulnerabilities stemming from inadequate understanding of specification semantics. Existing gray-box and black-box testing approaches lack semantic awareness.

papers.title: APFuzz: Towards Automatic Greybox Protocol Fuzzing
papers.abstract: Greybox protocol fuzzing is an effective technique for finding vulnerabilities in protocol implementations. We present APFuzz, a system for automatic greybox protocol fuzzing that requires minimal manual effort.

papers.title: MulCovFuzz: A Multi-Component Coverage-Guided Greybox Fuzzer for 5G Protocol Testing
papers.abstract: As mobile networks transition to 5G infrastructure, ensuring robust security becomes more important due to the complex architecture and expanded attack surface. We present MulCovFuzz, a multi-component coverage-guided greybox fuzzer for 5G protocol testing.

papers.title: BGPFuzz: Automated Configuration Fuzzing of the Border Gateway Protocol
papers.abstract: Telecommunications networks rely on configurations to define routing behavior, especially in the Border Gateway Protocol (BGP), where misconfigurations can lead to severe outages and security vulnerabilities.

papers.title: Synthesizing Precise Protocol Specs from Natural Language for Effective Test Generation
papers.abstract: Safety- and security-critical systems have to be thoroughly tested against their specifications. We propose a method to synthesize precise protocol specifications from natural language for effective test generation.

papers.title: ThreadFuzzer: Fuzzing Framework for Thread Protocol
papers.abstract: With the rapid growth of IoT, secure and efficient mesh networking has become essential. Thread has emerged as a key protocol for IoT mesh networks. We present ThreadFuzzer, a fuzzing framework specifically designed for the Thread protocol.
